GovernanceArticles 261 to 264

Transitional and Consequential Provisions

Kiswahili: Masharti ya Mpito na Matokeo

Sets the statutory schedule for enacting implementing legislation, repealing the former 1963 Constitution, and managing the transition to devolved governance.

Key constitutional takeaways

  • •Fifth Schedule sets strict deadlines for Parliament to enact implementing laws.
  • •Repeal of the former 1963 Constitution upon promulgation.
  • •Sixth Schedule governs transitional preservation of existing laws and judicial operations.

Articles in Chapter 18

Select an article to read its legal clauses and plain language meaning.

Clauses

(1)Parliament shall enact any legislation required by this Constitution to be enacted to govern a particular matter within the period specified in the Fifth Schedule, commencing on the effective date.

In plain language

Parliament was given strict timelines to pass laws operationalizing human rights, devolution, and judicial reforms.
